title: Annual regression concealed most of the DOISST step effect on trend-based feedback in five linear models for 1991-2011
abstract: We tested how the feedback estimator changes the effect of published SST step corrections in five linear atmosphere-model responses. In 1991-2011, DOISST raw-minus-corrected feedback differs by +0.405 W m-2 K-1 for a trend ratio but +0.031 for annual regression with the in situ correction. The CCI correction gives +0.400 and -0.052. The latter point sign reversal occurs in all five models, but the annual-regression interval includes zero. An exact covariance split explains the cancellation. For the CCI correction, the steps raise the share of annual SST variance in the trend from 0.394 to 0.693. The variance-weight contribution of -0.313 offsets slope contributions of +0.261. Fixed-date correction bootstraps retain positive trend-ratio effects but find no clear annual-regression effect. The OI v2 2001-2022 effect remains negative in both estimators and becomes uncertain after detrending. Thus a small regression difference cannot validate historical trend feedback. This extends a prior report of small full-record regression effects with a measured decomposition and conditional uncertainty. It reuses published monthly aggregates and does not detect new SST errors or estimate true climate feedback. Correction error, model structure, polar SST and global air-temperature normalization remain outside the test. Code, provenance, all statistics, bootstrap draws and an independent numerical audit support reproduction.

display.caption: Effects of published SST corrections depend on the feedback estimator. Points are raw minus corrected five-model mean feedback; bars are conditional 95% intervals with fixed correction dates and three-year residual blocks.
